newsitem.title: UK: Middle Eastern clean tanker rates ease, Caribs up.
newsitem.headline: Middle Eastern clean tanker rates ease, Caribs up.

text.p: Clean tanker rates out of the Middle East and in the Mediterranean weakened slightly this week, although some brokers said the outlook for next week was fairly positive.

"Owners are extremely bullish as the cocktail of high enquiry and low tonnage availability affords them every expectation of the markets remaining strong in all the main loading areas," shipping brokers Gibson wrote in their weekly report.

The star performer continued to be the Mediterranean region where rates for a 26,000 to 27,500 tonne naphtha cargo going cross-Med was seen commanding roughly W300, down from the W330 level seen last week.
Rates out of the Middle East were slightly lower with 55,000 tonne vessels bound for Japan reported fixed at around W212.50-215, against W227.5 seen at the end of last week.
Caribbean-upcoast U.S. coast rates were boosted by a fire at Tosco's 156,000 barrel-per-day refinery in Martinez, California on Tuesday.

"The lack of clean tonnage in the Caribbean... combined with a sudden and unexpected demand for jet fuel to the U.S. West Coast necessitated by an explosion at a San Francisco refinery caused rates to rise sharply," the Gibson report said.
Rates for 29,000 tonne vessels going up U.S. coast stood at around W300 on Friday against W200 at the end of last week.
